findings.title: Healthy real child lists are rejected because the judge assumes attachment-call order
findings.evidence: NAMES is light_rain, heavy_rain, light_wind, heavy_wind, sea, jungle, amb1, amb2, amb3, amb4. judge_complete requires the actual child-name vector to equal it exactly. However the real constructor inserts at the head; the unchanged characterized G11 case27 child vector is amb4, amb3, amb2, amb1, jungle, sea, heavy_wind, light_wind, heavy_rain, light_rain. Read-only inspection of the retained actual original case27 confirms those names; no new native run was performed. Scripted collaborators manufacture the forward vector and six forward terrain classes, so their healthy tests conceal the mismatch.
findings.impact: The first real healthy control fails before host-answer/consumer-word authority can be judged. Changed healthy modes likewise cannot pass. This is a witness error, not a production amplitude defect.
findings.requested_change: Use the genuine G11 list order and serialized ordinal/subtype/class facts. Make scripted healthy records and terrain questions match the real order, preserving the request-order-to-child-word mapping and distinct per-child changes. Do not reverse production physics or alter baselines. Retain a guard that wrong order/class mapping fails.

findings.title: The finite fixture and JSON protocol is not fully validated or reconciled
evidence: Lua collects exactly one env-sound-session row but never parses its selected-case i or session_unchanged_by_the_routine flag. Changing that row to another case or removing its flag does not affect success. Its before-child parser permits an empty vector and only compares after-list lengths; child ordinals and subtypes need not match the preceding vector, and rng_unchanged is not validated as 0/1.

Rust Child drops the serialized ordinal and subtype after only checking that they parse, so replacing numeric child ordinals/subtypes with duplicates leaves the mapping verdict unchanged. Facts ignores case.raw, children_before and restored and does not reconcile summary fields with the retained fixture text. Removing or changing only case.raw has no effect.

Facts requires the existence of a plan row but never validates its version/camera/completeness/selected-case facts. Ambient row n is neither parsed nor checked, and provider row ordering is not reconciled. A forged n or incomplete plan can therefore have the same verdict.

The fixed selected case27 has exactly one real call, but Lua accepts 1..8 and Rust accepts arbitrary positive calls; the recorder retains only the first four and judge_complete calls the last retained row the last answer. A coherent forged multi-call record can avoid the intended selected-case constraint.

Changed-mode judges do not check run.mode against the requested changed mode. The environment-variable documentation offers case6, while the public judge explicitly accepts only27; configuration and claimed coverage should agree.
findings.impact: The docs promise missing/truncated/dropped evidence cannot pass and mapping reaches the real corresponding children, but malformed or mismatched records can be treated as healthy. After fixing the real-order failure, the current finite guards still do not establish the stated protocol completeness.
findings.requested_change: Validate the actual finite G11 grammar before emitting case facts: selected case/label and exact call count, consecutive ordinal/subtype/class mapping across before and call vectors, one current-i session row with a 0/1 flag, valid required call/restoration fields. Have Facts require and reconcile the raw fixture record with JSON case fields, meaningful plan/envelope identity, provider n/order and counters, and expected mode; preserve refusal runs with no case row or post-stop observations. Add finite damaged-record guards for these concrete bypasses, and align optional-case documentation with supported judge scope. No new trace or physics framework is needed.

inspected_facts: The seven modes are bounded fixture controls. Providers are armed immediately before the selected G11 call and only op=ambient is altered; other operations delegate to the reference unchanged. There is no post-stop observer query or invented healthy completion after an engine guard.

Changed environment answers use finite distinct dyadics; terrain answers use distinct per-request amplitudes. The intended judge compares actual child words with recorded provider replies and requires a change from control, which is stronger than request counting. These checks should be retained while correcting the findings.

Specific refusal markers agree with the existing Lua bridge ambient.callback/ambient.answer/ambient.amplitudes grammar. Refusal checks require a matching alteration and a stopped engine with no case row; no general campaign, speaker, player or render claim is justified.

Output write/flush/close failures propagate and witness failures are rejected. The bounded runner uses one owned child with concurrent bounded pipe tails; the timeout guard uses the test executable rather than shell descendants. No new source-specific process-control blocker found in this bounded single-child scope.

Scripted provider/engine collaborators test bookkeeping, not native physics or ownership. Public-path SKIPPED is explicit when assets are absent. Any real evidence must pin the new embedded Lua/judge and unchanged d559 native separately; prior d559 payload identity is not this new witness execution.
